title: The sheaf of square-zero lifts has a quasi-coherent derivation action
statement: Let $f:V\to W$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a first order thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] with ideal $\mathcal I$, and let $a_0:T_0\to V$, $b:T\to W$ satisfy $fa_0=bi$. Regard $\mathcal I$ as an $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-module via $\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T_0}$, possible since $\mathcal I^2=0$. Put $\mathcal E=a_0^*\Omega^1_{V/W}$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Define the $\mathcal O_T$-module $\mathcal H=i_*\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(\mathcal E,\mathcal I)$: on an open $O\subset T$ its sections are the $\mathcal O_{T_0}|_{i^{-1}O}$-linear sheaf maps $\mathcal E|_{i^{-1}O}\to\mathcal I|_{i^{-1}O}$, with scalars acting through the quotient to $\mathcal O_{T_0}$. Then $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the rule sending $u:U\to T$ to the set of maps $a:U\to V$ satisfying $fa=bu$ and $a|_{U_0}=a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$, where $U_0=T_0\times_TU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], is a sheaf of sets $\mathcal L$. There is an action of the associated abelian etale sheaf $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] on $\mathcal L$, natural under restriction, such that for every $u:U\to T$ and every $a\in\mathcal L(U)$, the map $h\mapsto h\cdot a$ is a bijection $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)\to\mathcal L(U)$. Locally on $U$, if $h$ corresponds to the relative derivation $D$ with values in $\mathcal I\mathcal O_U$, the action replaces $a^\sharp$ by $a^\sharp+D$. No local or global existence of lifts is asserted.

source.place: Tags 061A (lemma-sheaf), 061C (lemma-action-sheaf), 061D (remark-special-case), restricted to schemes; quasi-coherence argument in Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), final paragraph. Scheme Zariski counterparts: more-morphisms.tex Tags 04FH, 04FJ, 04FK.

proof.text: By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $V$ is covered by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping into affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset W$ with $A$ finitely presented over $R$. On these charts $\Omega^1_{V/W}$ is the sheaf of $\Omega_{A/R}$ by [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. The latter module is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-ring-finite-presentation-differentials]. The affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] therefore makes $\Omega^1_{V/W}$ finitely presented as a sheaf. By [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation], $\mathcal E$ is finitely presented; no flatness of $a_0$ is needed. The ideal $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent on $T$ by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. As a module on $T_0$ it is also quasi-coherent: on $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$ with ideal $J$, it is the sheaf of the $A/J$-module $J$ because $J^2=0$, and localization agrees on principal opens. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent] applies to $K=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal E,\mathcal I)$ on $T_0$. Its closed pushforward $\mathcal H=i_*K$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated](1).

source.place: Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), final paragraph, using scheme Tags 01V3, 00RY, 01BQ, 01LA(10), 01QY

proof.text: For an etale covering $\{U_j\to U\}$, compatible maps $a_j:U_j\to V$ glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Their composites with $f$ equal $bu$ because equality of maps into $W$ can be checked on the same covering. The base-changed family $\{U_{j,0}=T_0\times_TU_j\to U_0\}$ is again an fpqc covering by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3), so the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] on it checks the equality with $a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$. Thus the glued map is a lift. Restrictions are composition and uniqueness is uniqueness of the glued map into $V$, proving that $\mathcal L$ is a sheaf.

Fix $u:U\to T$ etale, put $i_U:U_0\hookrightarrow U$, and let $u_0:U_0\to T_0$ be the projection. Etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. On affine charts $A\to B$, flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applied to $0\to J\to A\to A/J\to0$ identifies the ideal of $U_0$ with $J\otimes_AB=JB$, and $B/JB=B\otimes_A(A/J)$ is flat over $A/J$. Hence the ideal $\mathcal I_U$ is $u_0^*\mathcal I$, with square zero. Set $\mathcal E_U=u_0^*\mathcal E$. Because $\mathcal E$ is finitely presented, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] on each affine chart, together with the affine sheaf/module correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], identifies $u_0^*K$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal E_U,\mathcal I_U)$. The map is $c\otimes h\mapsto c(1\otimes h)$, so these local identifications agree on restrictions. The closed immersion $i$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]: over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening](4). The affine base-change theorem [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1) gives $u^*i_*K\simeq i_{U,*}u_0^*K$. Taking sections and using [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] therefore yields a canonical identification $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{U_0}}(\mathcal E_U,\mathcal I_U)$. It sends pulled-back module maps to the same maps on every chart; the displayed tensor formula proves compatibility with further etale restrictions.

Fix a lift $a\in\mathcal L(U)$ and let $g:U_0\to V$ be its reduction. The pullback composition isomorphism in [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies $\mathcal E_U=g^*\Omega^1_{V/W}$. By [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], its homomorphisms to $\mathcal I_U$ are homomorphisms $\Omega^1_{V/W}\to g_*\mathcal I_U$. By [lem-sfb-relative-differentials-sheaf-universal-property], these are exactly the $W$-derivations $D:\mathcal O_V\to g_*\mathcal I_U$. Both bijections commute with restriction. Thus step 3 identifies a coefficient $h$ with precisely such a relative derivation, with no choice of coordinates or finite free basis.

source.place: Tag 04FG (lemma-difference-derivation), equation-D and the adjunction immediately following it

proof.text: For the derivation $D$ of step 4, define a new ring-sheaf map by $a^\sharp+D$. On a local section $x,y$ of $\mathcal O_V$, its product is $a^\sharp(x)a^\sharp(y)+a^\sharp(x)D(y)+a^\sharp(y)D(x)$, since $D(x)D(y)=0$. The middle terms are the actions of $g^\sharp(x),g^\sharp(y)$ on $\mathcal I_U$, so Leibniz gives $(a^\sharp+D)(xy)=(a^\sharp+D)(x)(a^\sharp+D)(y)$. Additivity, preservation of one, and agreement over $W$ follow from the derivation identities. The map reduces to $g^\sharp$. To obtain the scheme morphism, cover $U$ by opens mapping under $a$ into affine opens $Q=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$. The topological spaces of $U_0$ and $U$ agree because their ideal is square zero. On each such open $P$, the ring map $A\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ gives a scheme map $P\to Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Its reduction is $g|_{P_0}$, so its underlying map is the one of $a|_P$. On overlaps the ring-sheaf maps are the same sum; they agree as maps into each affine target subchart by the same bijection, and hence glue. Denote the resulting lift by $h\cdot a$. Its ring-sheaf map is $a^\sharp+D$, so it is unique.

source.place: lemma-action-by-derivations following Tag 04FG; Tag 04FK (remark-special-case); omitted algebra-map check written out

proof.text: Conversely take another lift $c\in\mathcal L(U)$. Its underlying map is the same as that of $a$, since both reduce to $g$ and $U_0\to U$ is a homeomorphism. Their difference $D=c^\sharp-a^\sharp$ lands in $\mathcal I_U$. On sections, write $c^\sharp(x)=a^\sharp(x)+D(x)$. Expanding the product and using $\mathcal I_U^2=0$ gives $D(xy)=g^\sharp(x)D(y)+g^\sharp(y)D(x)$. The difference is additive and zero on sections from $W$, since $fa=fc=bu$. It is therefore a relative derivation of exactly the kind identified in step 4, and determines a unique $h\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)$. Addition and subtraction are inverse, so the orbit map $h\mapsto h\cdot a$ is bijective. Zero acts as the identity. Acting successively by coefficients with derivations $D_1,D_2$ gives $a^\sharp+D_1+D_2$; reductions and hence the module actions remain fixed throughout. This proves the additive action law.

source.place: Tag 04FG (lemma-difference-derivation), special case of zero target thickening; Tag 04FJ (lemma-action-sheaf)

proof.text: Every morphism $v:U\prime\to U$ in $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ restricts the coefficient of step 3 by the tensor formula there. Pullback of the ring-sheaf sum is the sum of the pulled-back maps, so $(h\cdot a)|_{U\prime}$ and $h|_{U\prime}\cdot a|_{U\prime}$ have the same ring-sheaf map and reduction. Uniqueness in step 5 makes them equal. Thus these actions define a sheaf action. If $\mathcal L(U)$ is empty, its action map is the unique map from $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}(U)\times\varnothing=\varnothing$ to $\varnothing$; all action identities on that object are vacuous. No existence claim has entered. Steps 5 and 6 give the specified formula and all orbit bijections.
